title: HTTP Status Codes for API Design

scenes.say: Why do status codes matter in API design? What do they actually tell your client apps?

scenes.label: 2xx
scenes.sub: 200 is OK, 201 means Created, 204 is No Content.
scenes.say: Status codes starting with two indicate success. Two hundred means okay, two oh one means created, and two oh four means no content.
For errors, four hundred means bad request, four oh one is unauthorized, four oh four is not found, four oh nine is conflict, and four twenty two is unprocessable entity.

scenes.title: POST /users
scenes.say: Say you post to slash users. Two oh one means success, four oh nine means the user exists, and four twenty two means validation failed.

scenes.question: Should you always return 200?
scenes.wrong: Yes, 200 is fine for all cases.
scenes.right: No, use the most specific status code for each response.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: should you always return two hundred? No. Use the most specific status code for each response.
